name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
summary: Adversaries may manipulate application software prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise. Supply chain compromise of software can take place in a number of ways, including manipulation of the application source code, manipulation of the update/distribution mechanism for that software, or replacing compiled releases with a modified version.

strategies.name: Detection of Compromise Software Supply Chain

analytics.name: Analytic 1853
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Compromise Software Supply Chain from documented management, network, or vetting evidence; treat state queries as periodic observations rather than real-time events. analytics.name: Analytic 1854
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Compromise Software Supply Chain from documented management, network, or vetting evidence; treat state queries as periodic observations rather than real-time events. Correlate Application Permission via Application Vetting [Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys]; Application State via Apple MDM [InstalledApplicationList / ManagedApplicationList]; OS API Execution via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: Launch services, extension-handling, or framework subsystem anomalies occur near install or first launch of recently updated trusted app on supervised device].
